title: Same brief, different burden
subtitle: Claude Opus 4.8 vs Codex gpt-5.6-sol on Driftfire custom boards
authority: analysis.md is authoritative; this file is its structured companion and index.html is its public presentation.

verdict.headline: Codex won this run
verdict.reason: It reached dependable integration with fewer human correctness interventions, cleaner boundaries, stronger network tests, and more effective visual verification.
verdict.developer_outcome: Codex became the developer's primary model after this run.

codex.head: d1166ded
codex.reported_coverage: 88.1% on last full verified head; later feel-tuning focused checks still in progress

phases.name: Identical opening brief
phases.summary: Both solved the data model; Codex carried it through rendering, local multitouch, and production transforms with less human intervention.

comparisons.requirement: Style, exclusions, component and texture rules

comparisons.codex: present in the first draft model

comparisons.claude: black screen, then gray rock and wrong background until device reports
comparisons.codex: real starfield and rock textures in first verified render

comparisons.claude: reported success while missing a device-visible failure
comparisons.codex: framebuffer matrix caught an invalid production-mapping test

phases.name: Product choices
phases.summary: Both added persistence and Uplink support, but the answers and resulting scope differed, so a flat requirement score is misleading.

phases.name: Later additions
phases.summary: Codex's live co-editing converges byte-identically and now handles joiner rotation. Claude's joiner remains unrotated and simultaneous remote drawing crashes on device.

claude: generation settings remained visible for the custom style
rock became gray while drawing and the background was not the starfield
Uplink skipped board creation and started an empty match
latest observed iOS build produced dots but not dragged lines
codex: first library UI did not match the established settings screen
first live co-edit canvas did not rotate for the joiner
first native iOS bridge caused a Web parse failure
codex_feel_calibration_not_correctness: make ordinary iOS width changes more responsive
retain initial contact width while dragging
make a flat thumb visibly wider

craft.claude: 658-line prescriptive implementation script with embedded code
58 added lines; app probes geometry and writes drawing state
craft.codex: 24 added lines; app delegates to CustomBoardFlow

craft.claude: 844-line screen owns input, paint, render, controls, persistence UI, and networking
craft.codex: editor, pure draft, flow, and network coordinator have explicit ownership

craft.claude: reuses DestructibleField painting and has antialiased fractional edges
craft.codex: pure GDScript authoring rasterizer must remain faithful to match terrain
rough until redirected to existing settings patterns

codex_unique_strengths: joiner presentation plus inverse screen-to-board mapping
tests.weakness: Claude's remote co-draw test injects board coordinates and compares solid-cell count, so it cannot catch wrong joiner mapping or different boards with equal area.

timing.method: Earlier session-log estimate: elapsed working span minus waits for user input, through the evaluator's comparable cutoffs.
timing.warning: Directional only. Later Codex iOS feel calibration is outside the cutoff, and logs do not measure focused human-equivalent labor.

quotes.speaker: developer
quotes.text: After this experience, Codex is clearly the winner, and it's going to become my primary model going forward.

quotes.speaker: evaluator, explicitly endorsed by developer
quotes.text: The user repeatedly became the integration test.

quotes.speaker: developer
quotes.text: Codex's PR description is better organized. I like the bullet points and the structure and the succinctness.

quotes.speaker: developer
quotes.text: Codex's plan seems more like a high-level checklist ... it should be read together with the design, whereas Claude's plan seems to supplant the design.

quotes.speaker: developer
quotes.text: Codex uses a lot fewer comments, which I like because its code speaks for itself.

caveats: The model tiers and effort settings were not matched.
The opening prompt was identical, but later product answers and requests differed.
Both agents used Claude and Codex reviewers, so final work is not unaided.
The environments and start times differed.
This is one feature, one developer, and one run—not a general benchmark.
Current heads include different later scope and should not be compared by diff size.
